shots.text: Taco John's legally owned the words Taco Tuesday.
A small chain from Wyoming, with about four hundred restaurants.
It registered the phrase in nineteen eighty-nine, in every state but New Jersey.
Even LeBron James tried to trademark it in twenty nineteen. The answer was no.
The government called the phrase too generic.
But Taco John's already had it, so for decades the taco night belonged to one company.
Then, in May twenty twenty-three, Taco Bell stepped in.
It asked the government to cancel the trademark, saying nobody should own a common phrase.
Taco Bell said it wanted no money. Only to set the words free.
Taco John's had a choice. Fight a giant, or walk away.
Two months later, on July eighteenth, it gave up the trademark in forty-nine states.
Its boss said, we're lovers, not fighters. The chain also gave forty thousand dollars to charity.
For over thirty years, a phrase on every menu in America had an owner.
